clue.text: I steal Act I and do so unexpectedly

indicators.note: something done unexpectedly comes out in an unforeseen order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A confession: the speaker pilfers the first act of a play, and does it without warning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unexpectedly' rearranges ACTI and DO. The definition is spoken by the answer itself: a bandit would say 'I steal'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dacoit is an armed robber of India or Burma, one whose trade is stealing.

clue.text: Half the district to aim to expand

indicators.note: half of the eight-letter word district means its first four letters

parts.note: an aim is an end, a goal

explanation.surface: A council plan to grow half the district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half' takes DIST, the first half of 'district'.
explanation.definitionFit: To distend is to swell out, enlarging from internal pressure.

clue.text: All material in the article with the editor being satisfied

parts.note: everything written in an article is its content
ED is the usual abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: An editor pleased with everything that made it into the piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone contented is happy with their lot, at ease and satisfied.

clue.text: Posh car at university in tip off for break in

indicators.note: one group of letters is placed inside the other
off in the sense of gone wrong, so the letters of tip are mixed up

parts.note: RR stands for Rolls-Royce, the archetypal posh car
U is short for university

explanation.surface: A grand car at college, crashed after a tip-off about a burglary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' signals the rearranging of 'tip', and 'in' the insertion; 'break in' looks like a burglary but is the definition, a bursting in.
explanation.definitionFit: To irrupt is to burst or force one's way in violently.

clue.text: Rapid movement to field giving a good return?

definitions.text: Rapid movement to field giving a good return?

parts.words: Rapid movement to field giving a good return?
parts.note: read as a stampede of prospectors to ground that might pay out in precious metal

explanation.surface: A dash onto a playing field that pays off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'field' suggests sport, but it means a goldfield, and the 'good return' is metal found there.
explanation.definitionFit: A gold rush is a sudden mass migration of prospectors to a new goldfield hoping for riches.

clue.text: Behead US fish in frenzied activity

indicators.note: to behead a word is to cut off its first letter

parts.note: the porgy is an American sea fish

explanation.surface: A command to decapitate an American fish in a frenzy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behead' cuts the P from PORGY.
explanation.definitionFit: An orgy, in its loose sense, is a bout of unrestrained indulgence or excess.

clue.text: Unprofitable situation not exactly lively!

definitions.meaning: a business venture that brings in nothing at all
taken literally the phrase is lifeless plus a loss, something with no spark

explanation.surface: A failing business that is hardly buzzing.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead loss is a total failure financially, and colloquially a dull, useless person or thing.

clue.text: League match

definitions.meaning: an alliance or association of members

explanation.definitionFit: A union is both an association of groups (a federation) and a marriage.

clue.text: Had noggin in parting, drunk, shamefaced

indicators.note: drunk means tipsy and disordered, so the letters are rearranged
parting means departing, so the word in leaves noggin

parts.note: taken as written: these two letters are removed

explanation.surface: Someone had a drink as a farewell, got drunk and felt ashamed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in parting' removes IN from NOGGIN, leaving NOGG; 'drunk' rearranges HAD and NOGG.
explanation.definitionFit: A hangdog look is guilty and abject, like a dog expecting punishment.

clue.text: Beginning of week right for a run in Australia

indicators.note: one letter is put in place of another

parts.note: Sunday is traditionally the first day of the week

explanation.surface: Starting the week by putting the right person in a run Down Under.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right for a' swaps the A in SUNDAY for R. In Australian cricket a sundry is an extra: a run not scored off the bat.
explanation.definitionFit: Australians call cricket extras sundries: runs credited from byes, wides and no-balls.

clue.text: Landed, disturbing river Niagara

indicators.note: disturbing means throwing into disorder, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone landed after a choppy trip down the Niagara.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbing' rearranges R and NIAGARA.
explanation.definitionFit: Landed and agrarian both relate to land ownership and agricultural estates.

clue.text: Wells' business partner takes in artist in muddle

indicators.note: takes in means swallows up, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Henry Wells and William Fargo founded Wells Fargo
RA is a Royal Academician, a common crossword artist

explanation.surface: A banker's associate takes on a painter and things get confused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes in' signals the insertion. 'Wells' suggests H G Wells the author, but it is the Wells Fargo company.
explanation.definitionFit: A farrago is a confused jumble or mixture.

clue.text: One-time English politician, one between left and right for instance

parts.note: ex means former
MP is a Member of Parliament

indicators.note: one letter sits between two others

parts.note: L is left
R is right
A means one

explanation.surface: A former English MP, someone between left and right, cited as an example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'between' puts A between L and R.
explanation.definitionFit: An exemplar is a model example, one given to illustrate a type.

clue.text: Produced exact copy of single in CD

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: single means alone, lone

explanation.surface: A hit single copied onto a compact disc.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the insertion; the CD in the clue is used letter for letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To clone something is to make a genetically or otherwise identical duplicate.

clue.text: Silly person in residence raised mode of transport

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other
in a down clue, raised means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a coot is a foolish person

explanation.surface: A fool living somewhere upmarket rides about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' signals the reversal (a down clue reads upward), giving SER, and 'in' the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: A scooter is a small motorbike or child's kick-propelled vehicle for getting around.

clue.text: A little backward preparing and handling computer gen

indicators.note: backward means the phrase is read from end to start

parts.note: a little is a tad
processing means preparing, as with food or film

explanation.surface: A slow learner getting ready to handle information on computers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backward' turns A TAD into DATA. 'gen' is British slang for information.
explanation.definitionFit: Data processing is the handling of information by computer, gen being slang for facts.

clue.text: See 15
One able to hold one's drink at table?

definitions.text: One able to hold one's drink at table?

parts.words: One able to hold one's drink at table?
parts.note: not a sober drinker but a container that keeps a bottle chilled at a meal

explanation.surface: A diner who can drink without getting drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hold one's drink' means not get drunk, but here it means literally contain a bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice bucket holds a wine bottle in ice to keep it cool on the table.

clue.text: Diligent, without depression, in open delicate work

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: free means open, unrestricted

indicators.note: without means lacking, so letters are taken away

parts.note: a dent is a depression in a surface

explanation.surface: A hard worker, not downhearted, doing delicate work in the open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' signals removing a depression from 'Diligent', leaving ILIG, and 'in' the insertion into the word for open.
explanation.definitionFit: Filigree is fine ornamental metalwork of twisted wire.

clue.text: Bond character of a certain station

definitions.text: Bond character of a certain station

parts.words: Bond character of a certain station
parts.note: a creation of author Michael Bond named after a London railway terminus

explanation.surface: A James Bond figure of some social standing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' suggests 007, but it is Michael Bond, the children's author; 'station' suggests social rank but is a London railway station.
explanation.definitionFit: Michael Bond's bear from Peru is found at, and named after, a London railway terminus.

clue.text: Pungent material produced when I park badly following reduced fee!

indicators.note: following means the rearranged letters come after the shortened fee
reduced means cut short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: pay is a fee or wage

indicators.note: badly means done wrong, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A hot spice turns up when the driver parks poorly after a cut-price charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' takes Y off PAY, and 'badly' rearranges I PARK into PRIKA.
explanation.definitionFit: Paprika is a hot red powdered spice made from dried peppers.

clue.text: See 19
The initially dearer but different tyre

indicators.note: different means altered, so the letters are rearranged
initially means take the first letter

explanation.surface: A remoulded tyre: it costs more at first but is not the same.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes T from 'The', and 'different' rearranges T and DEARER.
explanation.definitionFit: A retread is a used tyre given a new tread.

clue.text: Ingenious run out in opening

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: an adit is an entrance to a mine
RO is the cricket scoring abbreviation for run out

explanation.surface: A clever dismissal at the start of an innings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the insertion. An adit is a horizontal mine entrance, a crossword regular for 'opening'.
explanation.definitionFit: Adroit means skilful and clever, deft.

clue.text: Left in charge after bar is open

indicators.note: after means the following pieces come behind the bar

parts.note: a pub is a bar
L is left
IC means in charge

explanation.surface: A bar is opened, the staff left in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Public means openly known or accessible to all.

clue.text: Some gibe FO generated to cause confusion

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A jibe from the Foreign Office stirs up trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: FO is the Foreign Office, the British diplomatic ministry.
explanation.definitionFit: To befog is to obscure or bewilder, clouding the issue.

clue.text: Settle again to study sound

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it
sound means fair or valid

explanation.surface: Readjust your study to make it robust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'study' becomes READ, as in reading a subject at university.
explanation.definitionFit: To readjust is to settle or set things right once more.

clue.text: A garment could have it let out

definitions.meaning: a slit at the back of a jacket
to discharge or express, like feelings

explanation.surface: Letting out a dress.
explanation.definitionFit: A vent is a slit in a jacket's hem, and to vent is to release feelings.

clue.text: Nose within the frame for a coil

parts.note: within means in
a former is a frame on which a coil is wound

explanation.surface: A nose inside the frame, as on a coil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nose' is slang for a police informant.
explanation.definitionFit: A nose, in slang, is a spy or informant for the police.

clue.text: Written work that's evident on the course

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Written work that's evident on the course' (6), gives no parse for ROOKIE; it reads as a clue for another answer, and no source gives the printed clue.
annotationWithheld.clue: Written work that's evident on the course

clue.text: Greta with tie to be worn, or a feathered plume

indicators.note: worn means frayed or battered out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Greta is wearing a tie, or a feather headdress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be worn' rearranges GRETA and TIE.
explanation.definitionFit: An aigrette is a tuft of egret feathers worn as a head ornament.

clue.text: Put back without check explicitly formulated

indicators.note: without means lacking, so letters are removed

parts.note: reinstated means restored or put back
a rein is a check or restraint

explanation.surface: Restored without any restraint, as formally declared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without check' removes REIN from REINSTATED.
explanation.definitionFit: Stated means declared or set down clearly.
